simple.meaning: מָסַר (mâçar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to sunder , i.e. (transitively) set apart , or (reflex.) apostatize.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Numbers, beginning at Numbers 31:5. The surrounding contexts include Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מָסַר (H4560) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מָסַר (mâçar) / H4560 is traced through Numbers 31:5, Numbers 31:16 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to sunder , i.e. (transitively) set apart , or (reflex.) apostatize
definitions.full: H4560. masar [ מָסַר ] verb si vera lectio deliver up, offer (Late Hebrew מָסַר ; Aramaic deliver up, denounce, betray , מְסַר ; Hom ZMG xivi. 1892, 530 compare Sabean מסר take away ); — Qal Infinitive construct בי ׳לִמְסָרמַֿ֫עַל Num 31:16 offer (commit) a trespass against ׳י , but read לִמְעֹל , compare Thes Di (see 5:6 ; 2Chr 36:14 ). Niph`al Imperfect וַיִּמָּֽסְרוּ Num 31:5 delivered over to, assigned to (of warriors), read perhaps וַיִּסָּֽפְרוּ ( ᵐ5 . ἐξηρίθμησαν ) compare Thes. מָסֹ֫רֶת מֹסֵרוֺת, see אסר . [ מֹסָר ] see מוּסָר below יסר .

occurrences.englishText: So there were delivered, out of the thousands of Israel, a thousand from every tribe, twelve thousand armed for war.
Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against Yahweh in the matter of Peor, and so the plague was among the congregation of Yahweh.
